items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Harness and Hosted Agents Reach General Availability
items.summary_1line: Microsoft's Agent Framework now ships a supported runtime. Build 2026 brought the Agent Harness, the GitHub Copilot and Claude Agent SDK connectors, and the orchestration patterns to stable release; the harness and Fo...
items.editor_note: Harness and hosted agents reach general availability, adding a supported runtime plus GitHub Copilot and Claude Agent SDK connectors.

editorial.tldr: An independent open-source "agent harness" project resurfaced on Hacker News in mid-July as agent tooling converged on the term. Days later Microsoft shipped its own Agent Framework Harness, a supported runtime for hosting and running agents.
editorial.whats_new: Microsoft's Agent Framework Harness and hosted agents reached general availability on Aug 3, adding a stable runtime plus GitHub Copilot and Claude Agent SDK connectors first previewed at Build 2026.
editorial.why_it_matters: A harness is becoming a named, vendor-supported primitive for hosting and running agents rather than something teams build themselves — check whether the now-stable release covers your orchestration needs before rolling a custom equivalent.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you're hosting or orchestrating agents on Microsoft's stack, evaluate the now-GA Agent Framework Harness before building your own hosting layer — check whether its Claude Agent SDK connector already covers your integration.

status.detail: Shipped in preview Jul 23; runtime, Copilot connector, and Claude Agent SDK connector went stable Aug 3.

beats.headline: Microsoft releases the Agent Framework Harness
beats.summary: Microsoft's own runtime for hosting and running agents ships in preview.

beats.headline: Harness and hosted agents reach general availability
beats.summary: Build 2026's Agent Harness, the GitHub Copilot and Claude Agent SDK connectors, and the orchestration patterns go stable.

open_questions: Does the harness runtime's now-stable orchestration patterns extend beyond Microsoft's own ecosystem (Copilot, Claude Agent SDK) to other agent frameworks?
Do independent "harness" projects like Go Micro converge toward Microsoft's terminology and APIs, or does the term stay contested across vendors?
